headline: High: broad network-egress Firecrawl can feed untrusted web content into Kotaemon’s document pipeline, creating prompt-injection and cascading-error risk by default.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Firecrawl ingests web content and exposes scrape/search APIs, while Kotaemon processes HTML/PDF/chat-transcript inputs through a web UI and file workspace. That creates a plausible default bridge where attacker-controlled pages from agent_a become trusted content for agent_b. No shared channel is explicitly documented, so I avoid high and choose medium with uncertainty escalated.
conditions: IF agent_a output is copied into agent_b without sanitization
IF agent_b treats scraped HTML or markdown as instructions
IF both agents share a workspace or clipboard bridge
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of raw scrape output into agent_b
Strip instructions/HTML from agent_a outputs before passing them on
Use a provenance tag or allowlist for trusted sources
Review one sample handoff path end-to-end
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and provenance checks

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents handle API keys and broad network egress, and agent_b writes to ./ktem_app_data while agent_a handles web content and screenshots. If they share a workspace or operator account, sensitive material can move between them and out to third-party inference APIs. The profiles do not prove a shared filesystem, so medium is the highest supportable severity.
conditions: IF agent_a artifacts are stored in a directory readable by agent_b
IF agent_b sends imported documents to OpenAI/AzureOpenAI/Cohere/Groq
IF API keys are present in shared files or transcripts
mitigations: Separate working directories for each agent
Remove secrets from any shared inputs before handoff
Disable external API backends in agent_b for sensitive documents
Check file permissions on ./ktem_app_data
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent secret isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents support multiple instances and broad network egress, but the profiles do not show overlapping write access to the same mutable resource or shared git/database state. Without a documented shared write surface, a serious conflict is not established. I keep this low because the interaction is plausible but not evidenced.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same writable directory
IF both mutate the same external API-backed resource
IF the orchestrator provides no locking
mitigations: Assign distinct output directories
Serialize writes through one operator
Avoid concurrent edits to shared resources
Check for lock files before running both
requires-engineering: add resource locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: Firecrawl can produce scraped content and Kotaemon is a RAG/chat system that may render or reason over imported documents. If agent_b treats agent_a’s output as authoritative, errors or hallucinated facts can cascade into downstream answers. The profiles suggest the pathway but do not prove automatic action-taking, so medium fits better than high.
conditions: IF agent_b ingests agent_a outputs without verification
IF agent_a scrapes low-quality or adversarial pages
IF downstream users rely on agent_b answers for decisions
mitigations: Require source citations in agent_b outputs
Spot-check one retrieved answer against the original page
Block low-confidence pages from ingestion
Use a human review step for high-impact outputs
requires-engineering: add verification and provenance scoring

E_compliance.rationale: Both agents handle API keys and can send data to third-party model APIs, but the profiles do not specify residency, certifications, or DPA terms. Because compliance gaps are plausible yet undocumented, I cannot justify high; uncertainty pushes this to medium. The risk is mainly policy mismatch rather than a proven violation.
conditions: IF regulated data is processed through external model APIs
IF the deployment lacks a DPA or residency controls
IF retention settings differ between the two agents
mitigations: Confirm data-class handling rules for both agents
Disable external APIs for regulated inputs
Document retention and deletion settings
Route sensitive workloads to approved backends
requires-engineering: implement residency and retention controls
